about.title: West Covina Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: A hospital stay or clinic visit is supposed to leave you better off. When it doesn't, and the reason was a preventable error rather than an honest limit of medicine, California gives West Covina residents a path to hold the provider accountable. That path runs through MICRA, a set of rules that make medical negligence claims different from any other injury case in Los Angeles County. The clock is short: generally one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Before filing, your attorney must send the provider a 90-day notice of intent. And because a bad result on its own is not malpractice, almost every case depends on a qualified medical expert who can explain what the standard of care required and how it was breached. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect West Covina residents with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so no attorney fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated at a West Covina emergency room after a crash on the I-10 and my condition got worse. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California law, a bad outcome by itself is not malpractice; the question is whether the care fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done in the same situation. Emergency treatment after a collision on the San Bernardino Freeway or Azusa Avenue can be complicated, and a qualified medical expert would need to review your records to say whether a genuine error occurred.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no later than three years from the date the injury happened. Your attorney must also give the provider written notice at least 90 days before filing suit. These deadlines have exceptions and traps, so it is wise to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover?
items.answer: MICRA caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap increases each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost wages are handled differently. An independent attorney can walk you through how the current figures apply to your West Covina case.
